summary: Executed backend-only payment gateway regression suite for public config, secrets endpoint auth, cache headers, country-lock exemption, and Stripe key-prefix validation.
action_items: Keep monitoring data quality for legacy invalid Stripe publishable values stored historically (sk_ in publishable slot) even though public endpoints now suppress exposure.
critical_code_review_comments: GET /api/payment-gateway returns only public fields and applies Cache-Control: public, max-age=60 at backend origin (127.0.0.1:8001).
GET /api/payment-gateway/secrets correctly enforces X-PCStore-Secret and returns 401 for missing/wrong header.
PATCH /api/payment-gateway/settings rejects invalid Stripe key prefixes: publishable must start pk_, secret must start sk_, webhook must start whsec_.
Country middleware exempt list includes /api/payment-gateway, and origin tests confirm this route remains accessible while non-exempt route is blocked under forced country lock.
No Stripe/PayPal provider HTTP calls are present in payment gateway config/secrets handlers (configuration-read/write only).
test_credentials: Read from /app/memory/test_credentials.md; did not use or print real PCADMIN_INTERNAL_SECRET.
seed_data_creation: Used temporary dummy payment gateway values and temporary country access mutation; both singleton documents restored exactly via teardown fixtures.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Expanded /app/backend/tests/test_payment_gateway_settings.py with settings suppression check for legacy sk_ publishable values, Stripe prefix rejection tests, and origin-level country-lock exemption coverage for /api/payment-gateway.
rca of the issue: Initial exemption test against external ingress URL gave false-negative blocking signal because CF-IPCountry behavior differs through ingress/proxy path. Switching lock/exemption assertions to backend origin (127.0.0.1:8001) validated middleware behavior correctly and avoided platform-header interference.
